title: Taxes and household relief
intro: The questions below are about how much the federal government taxes companies and higher earners, and how much it pays to households with lower incomes. Other kinds of government spending are not part of it.
end0: Companies and higher earners are taxed much more heavily, and much more money goes to households with lower incomes.
end100: Companies and higher earners are taxed much less, and much less money goes to households with lower incomes.

title: Immigration
intro: These questions are about illegal immigration, asylum and other humanitarian protection: border and interior enforcement, who may enter or stay, and who is deported. Ordinary work, study and family visas are not part of it.
end0: Illegal entry is no longer a crime, interior immigration enforcement is abolished, no one is deported, and everyone living in the country illegally gets a path to citizenship.
end100: Everyone living in the country illegally is deported, there is no asylum or humanitarian admission of any kind, and citizenship or legal status obtained after an illegal entry is revoked.

title: Crime and punishment
intro: These questions are about how the state punishes crime and how heavily it polices: how long prison sentences are, whether the death penalty is used, what happens to a person once he has served his sentence, how many police there are and what is spent on them. How the police behave while on duty, who may be held responsible for what an officer does, and gun laws are not part of it.
end0: Prison sentences are cut far below today and mandatory minimum sentences are abolished, the death penalty is abolished, anyone who has served his sentence gets all his rights back including the vote, and the number of police is cut and the money spent on other public services instead.
end100: Prison sentences are raised far above today and mandatory minimums are extended to more offences, the death penalty is used for more crimes and carried out quickly, a conviction costs a man his vote for life, and many more police are hired and paid for out of other public services.
